title: Pick up and reach the rim in one dribble
description:
Place a ball by a cone on the three-point line. The player starts a few metres to the side, sprints to the ball and picks it up. Then a footwork move to turn and face the basket – for example a drop step or a step-through – followed by one single long dribble all the way to the lay-up.

After each attempt, move the cone with the ball a couple of metres further out, towards half-court. The further away, the further the ball has to be pushed out and the longer the strides. Switch sides so both hands get work. Finish back at the three-point line – it will feel easy, and that is exactly the feeling you want in a game.

Mind the travelling rule: the ball must leave the hand before the pivot foot lifts, otherwise it is a travel. It will look messy at first – keep trying. With several baskets, run one player per basket. The diagram is not to scale.

coachingPoints.text: Straight and long to the basket – no detours and no extra dribbles.
Push the ball out ahead towards the basket, not down by your feet.
The ball must leave your hand before your pivot foot lifts.
Dare to fail – further out should feel hard.

frames.note: The ball lies by the cone on the three-point line. A sprints over and picks it up.
A turns with a drop step, pushes the ball out in one long dribble and finishes with a lay-up.
The cone has been moved out a step at a time towards half-court. B goes from the other side to work the other hand.
